elements.content: Grammar focus: Mixed Conditionals for Past-Present Hypothesizing.

Core Rule: Use If + Past Perfect for past condition with Would + Base Verb for present result (Past -> Present), or If + Past Simple for permanent state with Would have + Past Participle for past result (Permanent -> Past).

If we had invested in 2010, we would be rich now.
If she were braver, she would have applied.
Had he listened, he would be safer today.
If I hadn't moved, I would still live there.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence links a past hypothetical action to a present result?
options: If we had adopted the protocol earlier, our systems would be secure today.
If we adopt the protocol, our systems will be secure.
